## 固定收益開篇論點

美國需求展現韌性，3位聚焦通膨的聯準會官員也對政策保持警戒，使兩份偏弱的6月物價報告所引發的漲勢受到抑制，美國公債7月16日小幅下跌。不過，殖利率升幅有限：2年期上升0.6個基點至4.142%，5年期上升0.7個基點至4.27%，10年期上升0.5個基點至4.554%，30年期則上升0.4個基點至5.084%。整條曲線近乎平行移動，2年期與10年期利差為41.2個基點，2年期與30年期利差為94.2個基點，單日變化都不大。

這種克制正是本交易日最鮮明的特徵。初領失業救濟金人數下降、零售銷售增加，費城聯準銀行製造業指數更升至近5年最高。達拉斯聯準銀行總裁 Lorie Logan 明確主張利率應略為提高；堪薩斯城聯準銀行總裁 Jeff Schmid 則警告，物價壓力仍然過於廣泛，不能因單月數據有利便予以忽視。儘管如此，美債僅回吐前兩個交易日漲幅的一小部分，利率選擇權交易員也繼續解除對近期升息的避險部位。

10年期殖利率的變動結構也支持這項解讀。實質殖利率上升1個基點至2.314%，損益兩平通膨率卻下降0.5個基點至2.24%。經濟活動數據保持強勁，使投資人要求略高的通膨調整後報酬；然而，即使伊朗周邊與荷莫茲海峽戰事再起，市場也未重新提高通膨補償。當日 WTI 下跌0.82%至$78.95，布蘭特原油下跌0.85%至$84.23；即便航運持續受阻，兩者一週漲幅仍約為10%。

市場因而把7月決策與後續政策路徑分開看待。交換市場對7月29日會議的升息定價約為3個基點，相當於升息25個基點的機率約13%，低於本週初的約40%；12月合約仍反映約29個基點的升息幅度。6月通膨降溫，已降低立即升息的可能性，但週四的成長數據與聯準會官員談話，也不支持把升息循環視為已明確結束。

風險性資產則對人工智慧建設規模及其融資方式發出另一項警訊。即使台積電調高營收及資本支出展望，費城半導體指數仍下跌4.29%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.62%，S&P 500也下跌0.51%。台積電的強勁業績未能壓過市場疑慮：美國4大 AI 業者今年支出可能超過$7,250億，但何時轉化為營收仍不明朗。這個問題對債市的重要性也日益提高；科技業借款人在投資級市場的占比持續增加，Oracle 的 S&P 評等僅比非投資級高一級，另有一筆大型槓桿再融資案必須大幅改善條件，才有望獲得市場承接。

## 強勁數據抑制通膨降溫行情

當日公布的美國數據顯示，經濟目前動能穩健，但各產業表現並不均衡。6月零售與餐飲服務銷售初值較前月增加0.2%至$7,686億，較去年同期成長6.7%。5月月增幅也由0.9%上修至1%，墊高比較基期，因此6月溫和的整體增幅並不意味消費者全面退縮。

細項表現尤其重要。扣除汽車的銷售下降0.2%，但扣除汽油後增加0.7%，同時排除汽車與汽油的指標則上升0.4%。汽車經銷商與非店面零售商的銷售都增加1.9%，加油站營收下降5.3%，餐飲服務銷售僅成長0.1%。汽油營收減少壓低整體數字，卻未顯示可自由支配消費普遍轉弱。

勞動市場數據也釋出短期韌性訊號。截至7月11日當週，初領失業救濟金人數減少8,000人至20.8萬人，前值修正為21.6萬人；4週移動平均減少4,750人至21.425萬人。截至7月4日當週，續領人數減少1.6萬人至180.5萬人，但其4週移動平均小幅升至181.1萬人；投保失業率維持在1.2%。初領與續領人數同步下降，並未讓聯準會看到限制性利率已造成就業突然惡化的明顯證據。

費城聯準銀行調查呈現當日最強的即期成長訊號。7月一般商業活動指數由10.3躍升至41.4，創近5年最高；新訂單指數由27.3升至37，出貨指數由14.9升至33.7，就業與平均工時指數也分別維持在10與14的正值。

然而，價格指標未呈現6月全國通膨數據的改善。支付價格指數由53.2升至53.9，收取價格指數由20.3升至27.4。前瞻指標則不如當期數據強勁：未來6個月預期活動指數由50.2降至34.4，計畫資本支出指數由41.2降至30.1。因此，這份調查強化了目前需求與生產流程價格壓力仍強的論點，卻未顯示製造商預期同樣的加速態勢將持續下去。

5月企業數據同樣反映名目交易活動強勁。製造業與貿易銷售較4月增加2.1%，較去年同期增加11.9%，達$2.135兆；庫存月增僅0.3%、年增3.1%，至$2.736兆，使庫存銷售比由一年前的1.39降至1.28。銷售成長快於庫存累積，顯示目前經濟活動並非靠非自願性庫存增加維持。

房市仍是最明顯的反向力量。6月數值修正為36後，NAHB／富國銀行房市指數再下降2點至34，連續15個月低於40，為2012年以來最長紀錄。當前銷售指數降至37，未來6個月銷售預期降至43，潛在買方來客指數則滑落至23。37%的建商降價，平均降幅為6%，另有63%提供促銷優惠。即使消費、製造業與勞動市場保持韌性，融資成本與負擔能力仍持續壓抑這個對利率敏感的產業。

這組數據說明，美債殖利率為何僅小幅上升，沒有逆轉先前由通膨數據帶動的漲勢。經濟活動較強，意味政策若比市場先前預期更早結束限制性立場，代價也會提高；但這批數據仍未推翻偏弱的 CPI 與 PPI。房市依舊疲弱，製造業前景預期降溫，零售銷售整體數字偏低又有部分來自汽油價格下跌，並非支出普遍崩跌或全面加速。

利率選擇權部位也反映這項區別。美國交易時段內，市場繼續賣出會因政策利率上升而受益的9月與12月選擇權；先前未平倉量下降顯示，交易員是在平掉既有避險，而非單純建立新部位。7月升息機率仍低，12月前的升息定價則由本週初43個基點降至約29個基點。市場是在降低對升息速度與路徑的信心，並未改為定價降息循環。

Logan 對這種偏樂觀解讀提出最直接的質疑。這位今年擁有聯邦公開市場委員會投票權的達拉斯聯準銀行總裁表示，由於通膨似乎尚未持續回到2%，略為提高利率更能平衡風險。她承認6月通膨有所改善，若住房及非住房服務價格進一步降溫，結果可能更為有利；但這條路徑的前提，是近期能源壓力不能再起，後續需求也不能轉強。

本週油價反彈，加上週四經濟活動數據偏強，使這項前提格外重要。Logan 表示，單月通膨緩解並不足夠；AI 投資對需求的影響已經出現，其生產力效益的規模與實現時間卻仍不確定。換言之，AI 資本支出熱潮已透過設備、營建、電力與勞動力形成當前需求，政策判斷不能先假設未來的生產力提升會立即抵銷這些壓力。

Schmid 則提出另一項警告。這位堪薩斯城聯準銀行總裁稱通膨是他最主要的關切，並表示物價壓力不僅來自能源，也遍及包括食品在內的廣泛商品與服務。他認為，6月數據改善仍不足以構成趨勢；判斷通膨是否持續時，除了供給衝擊，也必須考慮強勁需求。同時，他認為勞動市場處於平衡狀態、經濟成長具有韌性，進一步支持聯準會可專注處理物價，而不必因就業突然轉差作出反應。

副主席 Philip Jefferson 在固定收益市場收盤後發布的談話中，提出較具條件性的訊號。他認為，目前政策位置足以在通膨下降之際支持就業；但若實際通膨未能很快開始降溫，就可能需要重新考慮政策立場。Jefferson 強調，AI 可能同時造成方向相反的需求與供給衝擊，兩者發生的時間對政策相當重要；他也把能源衝擊傳導至較長期通膨預期的可能性列為關鍵風險。這些談話並未影響已完成的美債收盤，但若6月的改善無法延續，保留升息路徑的官員陣容已進一步擴大。

殖利率變動不大之際，美債現券交易也轉淡。FINRA 記錄到32萬6,681筆交易，面額合計$9,053億，較7月15日減少14.7%；名目附息債交易面額下降19.1%至$6,820億。剩餘期限超過3年、至多5年的券種成交額減少29.9%，超過7年、至多10年的券種則減少15.9%。這些是雙向交易活動指標，但仍可看出，週四的溫和回吐不同於先前通膨重新定價期間較為熱絡的參與程度。

短端供給則持續獲得現金需求承接。美國財政部標售$1,100億4週期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.660%，投標倍數2.57倍；另標售$1,000億8週期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.650%，投標倍數2.84倍。間接投標人在較短天期標售中獲配$549.49億競標額，在較長天期標售中獲配$654.70億。兩批國庫券均於7月21日交割。由於缺少發行前交易參考，結果無法判定定價偏貴或偏便宜；不過，在附息債市場爭論政策路徑之際，短端融資並未顯露明顯壓力。

## 韓國轉向緊縮，日本通膨預期升高

韓國展開新一輪緊縮循環，決策獲一致通過，將7天期附買回利率提高25個基點至2.75%。這是2023年1月以來首次升息，結果符合彭博經濟學家調查的所有預測。韓國自2024年底以來已降息4次，因此本次行動代表政策方向逆轉，而不是既有升息行動的延續。

韓國央行總裁 Shin Hyun Song 維持緊縮傾向，卻未暗示下次升息時間或最終利率高點。他表示，接下來每次會議都有採取行動的可能，後續決策將取決於通膨、成長與金融穩定的新證據。交換市場定價顯示，未來6個月至少還會升息2次，但 Shin 並未認同加快升息的時程。

政策理由不只在於整體通膨。Shin 表示，韓國央行5月預測2026年經濟成長2.6%，如今看來偏低；由於出口、投資與消費均強於預期，8月將大幅上修。政府已把預測提高至3%，國際貨幣基金也將預測調升至2.6%，上修幅度居30個主要經濟體之首。

6月消費者通膨升至3.2%，為逾2年最快，政府預計全年平均為2.6%。Shin 表示，韓元疲弱將繼續推高進口價格，經濟活動轉強也可能帶來額外的需求型通膨。半導體出口熱潮使韓國2026年前5個月的經常帳盈餘，已超過2025年全年的歷史紀錄；第1季經濟則成長1.8%。

韓國央行認為，這一輪晶片景氣比過往出口上升週期更具結構性，因為 AI 需求正使半導體由傳統最終產品轉變為基礎設施。Shin 指出，相較晶片公司股價的短期變化，晶片價格更能反映韓國的貿易條件與經濟成長。這項區別在週四尤其重要：即使台積電季度獲利成長77%並上調展望，全球半導體類股仍遭到拋售。

出口熱潮帶來的效益並不平均。就業仍然疲弱，資本密集的半導體生產所創造的工作機會，少於其產出通常應帶來的水準。金融穩定風險也強化升息理由：首爾公寓價格已連續76週上漲，家庭借款再度加速，官員並警告槓桿投資可能放大失衡。

決策與記者會後，韓國債券反而上漲。3年期殖利率下降4個基點至3.83%，10年期殖利率同樣下降4個基點至4.29%。這項反應符合升息早已在預期內，而政策指引只保留按季或依數據緊縮的可能，並未承諾加快行動。若投資人原先為更強硬的訊號預作準備，升息仍可與殖利率下降並存。

日本也出現與通膨預期相關的警訊。家庭預期未來5年年均通膨為10.8%，創日本央行2006年開始統計以來最高，不過中位數仍為5%。日本央行執行理事 Koji Nakamura 再次表示，上行風險偏高，延後調整政策最終可能拖累經濟。基準利率在6月升至1995年以來最高後，目前為1%；交易員認為10月前再度升息的機率約為66%。

這份調查也顯示政策正常化的代價。認為利率已經過高的家庭占24%，創歷史最高。日本央行因此必須在異常高漲的主觀通膨感受與借款成本敏感度升高之間權衡，下次政策決策訂於7月31日。

日本短端標售提供了實際需求指標，但未能解決這項政策取捨。1年期國庫貼現券標售接受¥2.136兆競標及¥6,644億非競標投標。最低得標價格98.801，對應殖利率1.2168%；加權平均殖利率為1.2066%，最低得標價的分配比例為73.8823%。證券於7月21日發行，2027年7月20日到期。

另一項流動性增進操作則針對剩餘期限1至5年的已發行 JGB，接受¥6,990億投標，競標總額為¥2.679兆。最高得標利差為負0.001%，該利差的分配比例為70.1674%；平均得標利差為負0.004%。這項結果反映合格的2年、5年、10年、20年與30年期舊券需求，並不提供新指標券殖利率訊號。

英國數據呈現較疲弱的政策組合。4月實質國內生產毛額經修正後下降0.1%，5月則成長0.1%。截至5月的3個月產出成長0.7%，較去年同期增加1.1%。服務業月增0.3%，但生產部門萎縮0.5%，營建業下降0.8%，顯示復甦依賴服務業，並未廣泛分布於各產業。

英格蘭銀行副總裁 Sarah Breeden 認為，經濟活動疲弱、勞動市場有閒置空間，降低了能源通膨再起後固化於薪資與國內物價的風險。她在過去3次會議都隨多數決支持將政策利率維持在3.75%，戰爭前則曾主張降息。Breeden 表示，若物價形成回饋循環，她會支持升息；但在借款成本已壓抑家庭與企業的情況下，單憑石油衝擊並不足以支持升息。5月產出的組成支持她的審慎立場，但布蘭特原油的單週漲幅仍使第二輪效應風險存在。

## AI 借款提高信用市場門檻

Oracle 把 AI 投資造成的融資壓力直接帶進投資級債市。由於規模$2,500億的資料中心擴建計畫消耗現金的速度快於營收流入，S&P Global Ratings 將公司信評降至 BBB-，只比非投資級高一級。Moody’s 則維持負向展望，中期內仍可能進一步降評。

Oracle 的支出與收入時間落差異常龐大。最近4季扣除資本支出後，公司消耗逾$200億現金；S&P 估計，下一會計年度自由現金流缺口可能擴大至$420億。預計資本支出至少到2029會計年度仍將持續增加。公司已累積大量合約未履約餘額，但營收會隨時間逐步認列，營建與設備成本卻必須預先支付。

Oracle 債券反映的風險已高於評等標籤本身所顯示的程度。其10年期債券殖利率約6.4%，接近同類 BB 級債券的6.7%，且遠高於10年期 BBB 級曲線的5.7%。若有2家評等機構將其降至非投資級，Oracle 可能成為規模較小的美國高收益債市場中最大發行人，不僅可能推高借款成本，也會迫使新的投資人群體吸收這些債務。

公司表示，維持投資級評等仍是資本配置的最高優先事項。本會計年度預計透過債券與股票籌集約$400億，包括先前已公布的$200億市價發行股票計畫。Oracle 於2月發行了$250億投資級債券，目前約有$1,170億債券納入彭博美國公司債指數，是僅次於 Amazon 的第二大非金融業成分發行人。

集中度使融資問題更加嚴重。S&P 估計，Oracle 的$6,380億剩餘履約義務中，約有一半與 OpenAI 有關。這些待履行合約提供了未來營收路徑，卻也使融資計畫高度暴露於單一大型客戶，以及已簽約 AI 需求轉化為現金流的速度。Alphabet 與 Meta 以內部資金支應投資的能力較強；Oracle 則可能必須削減資本支出、增發股票，或接受更高槓桿。

整體債券指數對同一週期的暴險也愈來愈高。依是否納入私募證券而定，超大規模雲端業者債券約占投資級市場市值的4%至5%。這些公司通常以較寬利差發行較長天期債券，因此 Barclays 計算顯示，其債券占指數「存續期間乘以利差」風險的8.3%。若納入範圍更廣的 AI 相關發行人，比重將升至11.4%，超過過去主導發債市場的6家大型銀行。

如此龐大的風險占比，使追蹤基準的投資人難以忽視 AI 融資週期。新增科技債供給必須與銀行、工業公司及政府爭奪有限的長天期資金承接能力。高評等超大規模雲端業者的債券可以提供具吸引力的利息收益，但若持續出現意外供給，市場可能要求更大的發行讓利，並把成交利差上升的影響擴散至科技業借款人以外。

Cotality 顯示，當槓桿較高、現金流較弱時，融資門檻會多快上升。這家房地產資料公司在需求不足後，考慮提高一筆$53億再融資案部分債券的殖利率。擬議第一順位留置權債券的殖利率，可能由8%區間中段調高至最高9.5%；第二順位留置權券次則可能由11%調至約12%，並以低於面額發行。投資人也在討論加強契約文件保障，但尚未敲定任何修改。

該公司債務約為獲利的8倍，S&P 評等低於投資級6級。截至3月31日，公司約持有$5,500萬現金；由於自由現金流仍非常有限，預計將依賴循環信用額度。這筆交易原定週四定價，目的是為 Stone Point Capital 與 Insight Partners 以$60億收購公司時使用的債務再融資。交易延後，且可能需要進一步讓利，顯示即使整體信用環境的利差偏緊，大型槓桿交易也無法憑此克服流動性不足與槓桿過高的問題。

Aston Martin 的債權人則在防範另一種融資風險。由 Arini Capital Management、BlackRock 與 Sculptor Capital Management 領頭的基金聘請 Jefferies 擔任顧問，原因是相對寬鬆的債券文件可能容許公司透過新增借款，使既有債權的受償順位居後。這個團體持有公司2029年到期、等值$18.5億債券的多數部位，已簽署合作協議，並提出討論新融資與整體資本結構的意願。

Aston Martin 過去仰賴注資支撐流動性，4月另取得£5,000萬股東貸款。產品延誤、品質問題、中國需求疲弱與美國關稅，都加深債權人的疑慮，擔心後續融資可能利用擔保品或架構條款，使現有債券持有人處於不利地位。目前接洽仍屬準備性質，並非已達成重整協議；但問題已由一般性的資產負債表疑慮，發展為有組織的債權人行動。

芝加哥將逾期停車罰款變現的努力也陷入停滯。由於雙方無法就服務範圍達成協議，美國銀行已停止擔任一項約$10億應收款出售案的配售代理。這項計畫原擬籌集至少$8,900萬，以協助填補市府預算缺口，但官員指出，潛在買方可能面臨隱私、法律與聲譽風險。即使多項稅收優於計畫，交易遲無進展也是預估$9,000萬年中收入缺口的原因之一。

掛牌信用債的整體價格相對穩定。LQD 下跌0.07%，HYG 下跌0.01%，JNK 上漲0.01%，EMB 則下跌0.15%。這些細微變化並未顯示出與半導體股跌勢相當的全面重新定價。更重要的訊號來自個別發行條件：高槓桿再融資需要大幅提高殖利率，Oracle 的 AI 擴張已消耗其評等緩衝，而 Aston Martin 債權人也在任何新交易削弱其地位之前開始組織行動。

## 戰爭風險擴大主權債分化

美國與伊朗戰事再起，對中東主權信用債的影響，比對美債通膨補償更為直接。美國總統 Donald Trump 警告停火可能結束後一週，中東主權債平均利差擴大約20個基點，來到較美債高402個基點，為2022年10月以來最寬，也促使今年以來的利差增幅達到2018年後最快。

自戰爭爆發以來，中東美元債已成為新興市場表現最差的區域類別。區內政府債券相較其他開發中國家主權債，多提供163個基點的殖利率。這波重新定價逆轉了4月暫時停火後逾50個基點利差收窄的一部分。

安全情勢週四再次惡化。美國在伊朗主要石油碼頭附近攻擊一艘受制裁的超級油輪，是恢復封鎖以來首次在當地攻擊船隻。荷莫茲海峽可觀察到的商業船舶稀少，且大多是與伊朗有關、使用德黑蘭核准北方航線的船隻。印度下令船東停止派遣該國海員航經海峽，亞洲液化天然氣現貨價格也升至3月以來最高。

不過，原油在連續3天大漲後，紐約收盤仍小幅下跌。布蘭特原油一週漲幅維持在10.39%，WTI 為9.53%，單日回落並未使能源市場恢復至升級前的狀態。美元指數上漲0.23%，黃金期貨下跌1.44%至$3,985.60，VIX 則上升6.76%至16.73。殖利率與美元走高，壓過地緣政治帶來的黃金避險需求；股票波動則最明顯地集中於科技類股。

塞內加爾反映的主權債問題，主要並非外部流動性，而是財政償付能力。Citigroup 估計，若重整後債券殖利率分別為11%與9%，美元債持有人每$1可收回$0.43至$0.50。現有債券成交價介於面額的$0.51至$0.54，2048年到期債券在倫敦報$0.5170，高於 Citi 情境區間的下緣。

塞內加爾債務接近國內生產毛額的130%，國際貨幣基金計畫也已暫停。當局大致仍反對債務重整，但 Lazard 獲任命為財務顧問，加上區域市場較長天期證券需求轉弱，已加劇市場對必須展開談判的猜測。塞內加爾主權債利差較美債高近1,500個基點，是 JPMorgan 指數所涵蓋非洲主權發行人中最嚴重的困境水準。

Citi 認為，塞內加爾與尚比亞、迦納不同，眼前問題在於財政與債務可持續性，而不是國際收支短缺。但這項差別不會降低重整對債券持有人的代價。該行判斷，若塞內加爾繼續推動 IMF 支持的調整方案，就必須大幅削減債券名目本金；國內政治則會影響談判是否在今年啟動。

長天期債券投資態度的轉變也不限於陷入困境的借款人。Hoisington Investment Management 以逾30年來長期看多美債著稱，如今認為財政赤字擴大、資本需求增加，以及長期通膨區間升高，都指向長期殖利率走升。其投資組合的有效存續期間，已由9月底的20.88年降至3月底的4.7年，至6月30日更降至不足1年。

Hoisington 估計長期通膨均衡區間約為3.5%至4.5%，而且相當可能出現高於5%的階段，並認為投資人正要求美債提供更高的期限溢價。這是資產管理人的結構性觀點，不是對週四小幅行情的描述；然而，即使6月通膨數據有利，市場仍不願把30年期殖利率明確壓至5%以下，與此看法一致。長債收在5.084%，當日雖僅小幅上升，月內仍累計上升10.4個基點。

## 後續市場意義

下一批美國數據將於7月17日公布。6月進出口價格及房屋開工訂於美東時間08:30發布，工業生產與產能利用率在09:15公布，密西根大學消費者信心初值則於10:00出爐。貿易價格可顯示能源、航運與關稅成本是否已反映在進出口價格，並可能進一步傳導至消費者通膨；房屋開工將檢驗建商信心疲弱是否已反映於營建活動，工業生產則可判斷費城聯準銀行指數大升是否代表更廣泛的製造業加速。

聯準會官員強調能源衝擊再起可能轉為持久後，密西根大學的通膨預期指標尤其重要。若通膨預期保持穩定，將支持市場週四未重新提高10年期通膨補償的決定。若通膨預期上升，且消費者信心與生產數據同樣穩健，則會強化 Logan 與 Schmid 的疑慮：在需求增強、能源到岸成本上升下，6月有利的通膨結果可能無法延續。

歐元區6月調和通膨終值訂於7月17日歐洲中部夏令時間11:00公布。歐洲央行正評估能源價格上升是否擴散至商品、服務或薪資設定，因此數據組成將影響7月23日的決策。7月21日公布的歐洲央行銀行放款調查，則會在利率決策及記者會前，進一步提供第2季授信標準、貸款需求，以及銀行對第3季看法的證據。

中國將於7月20日中國標準時間09:00設定1年期與5年期貸款市場報價利率。此次定價在房地產與投資數據疲弱後進行，可觀察政策制定者是否願意透過銀行貸款利率傳遞更寬鬆的融資條件。日本7月17日的3個月期國庫券標售，將檢驗短期日圓資金需求；但更重要的長天期事件，是7月22日約¥3,000億的40年期 JGB 增額發行。標售之際，日本家庭通膨預期創新高，日本央行仍維持緊縮傾向，且有更多家庭認為利率已經過高。

美國財政部供給將於7月20日恢復，包括$920億13週期國庫券及$790億26週期國庫券，兩者都在7月23日交割；7月21日另將標售$950億6週期國庫券。長天期考驗則是7月22日美東時間13:00增額發行$130億20年期公債。該券票息5%，7月24日交割，2046年5月15日到期。在30年期殖利率仍高於5%，且民間 AI 借款爭奪長天期資金承接能力之際，此次標售將檢驗市場對期限風險的需求。

企業融資進度也將提供相互對照的指標。Cotality 擬議再融資案的第一順位留置權債券殖利率，已由8%區間中段往最高9.5%調整，契約保障可能改善，第二順位留置權債券殖利率則會更高。這家公司能否完成$53億交易，以及最終能提供哪些保障，將顯示即使整體信用債基金價格變化不大，高槓桿借款人仍需讓利多少。

美國與伊朗衝突，是市場區分「已實現通膨轉弱」與「前瞻通膨轉強」所面臨的最直接威脅。荷莫茲海峽船舶稀少，美國也在伊朗出口碼頭附近發動攻擊，但原油尚未再次出現單日暴漲；布蘭特與 WTI 的一週漲幅仍約為10%。即使聯準會7月29日維持利率不變，若干擾持續，後續通膨數據、企業利潤率與主權風險仍會受到影響。

對美債而言，核心考驗已不再是6月 CPI 與 PPI 是否已消除7月升息的大部分理由，因為市場定價已反映這項判斷。真正的問題是，消費具有韌性、申領失業救濟金人數偏低，以及當前製造業活動強勁，是否會讓官員保留或落實今年稍晚升息的可能。若廣泛通膨進一步降溫、通膨預期維持穩定，7月16日殖利率僅小幅回升便屬合理；若物價壓力再度擴散、能源壓力持續，或經濟活動數據連續偏強，目前近期升息機率偏低、但12月前仍定價超過一次25個基點升息的組合，將更難維持。

overall_summary.headline: 美國需求展現韌性，美債仍僅小幅回吐通膨降溫行情
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美債小幅下跌，但曲線近乎平行且變動克制：2年期殖利率上升0.6個基點至4.142%，10年期上升0.5個基點至4.554%，30年期上升0.4個基點至5.084%。零售銷售、初領失業救濟金人數及費城聯準銀行調查均顯示需求具有韌性；Lorie Logan 與 Jeff Schmid 則警告，單月通膨數據有利仍不足以解除疑慮。儘管如此，交換市場對7月29日會議的升息定價僅約3個基點，12月前則約為29個基點。

10年期實質殖利率上升1個基點，損益兩平通膨率則下降0.5個基點，顯示投資人要求較高的通膨調整後報酬，卻未重新提高通膨補償。美國與伊朗戰事再起、荷莫茲海峽航運受阻之際，油價收盤下跌，但一週漲幅仍約為10%。

AI 融資則發出另一項風險訊號。市場對支出規模及回報不確定性的疑慮升高，半導體股大幅下跌；同時，Oracle 的評等緩衝縮小，Cotality 的槓桿再融資案也必須大幅改善擬議條件。
overall_summary.summary: 零售、勞動與製造業數據強勁，加上聚焦通膨的聯準會官員談話，使今年稍晚升息的可能性得以保留；但7月立即升息的理由並未明顯增強，美債殖利率因此只小幅走高。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries edged lower on July 16 as resilient U.S. demand and a trio of inflation-focused Federal Reserve officials checked the rally generated by two softer June price reports. The move was small: the 2-year yield rose 0.6 basis point to 4.142%, the 5-year added 0.7 basis point to 4.27%, the 10-year increased 0.5 basis point to 4.554%, and the 30-year rose 0.4 basis point to 5.084%. The nearly parallel adjustment left 2s10s at 41.2 basis points and 2s30s at 94.2 basis points, both little changed on the day.

That restraint was the session’s defining feature. Initial jobless claims fell, retail sales increased, the Philadelphia Fed’s manufacturing index surged to its strongest level in nearly five years, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan explicitly favored modestly higher rates. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid separately warned that price pressure remained too broad to dismiss after one favorable month. Yet the Treasury market gave back only a fraction of the previous two sessions’ rally, with rate-option traders continuing to unwind protection against an imminent increase.

The composition of the 10-year move reinforced that interpretation. The real yield rose 1 basis point to 2.314%, while the breakeven inflation rate fell 0.5 basis point to 2.24%. Investors required slightly more inflation-adjusted return as the activity data remained firm, but did not rebuild inflation compensation despite renewed fighting around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. Oil declined on the day—WTI by 0.82% to $78.95 and Brent by 0.85% to $84.23—even though both remained roughly 10% higher over the week and shipping disruption continued.

The market was therefore distinguishing the July decision from the later policy path. Swaps priced about 3 basis points of tightening for the July 29 meeting, equivalent to roughly a 13% chance of a quarter-point increase, down from about 40% at the start of the week. December contracts still incorporated around 29 basis points of tightening. June inflation relief had made an immediate increase less likely, but Thursday’s growth data and Fed commentary argued against treating the tightening cycle as conclusively finished.

Risk assets supplied a separate caution around the scale and financing of the artificial-intelligence buildout. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 4.29%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.62%, and the S&P 500 declined 0.51% even after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing raised its sales and capital-spending outlook. TSMC’s strong results could not overcome concern that the four largest U.S. AI operators may spend more than $725 billion this year before the revenue payoff is clear. That issue is increasingly important for bonds as well as equities: technology borrowers are occupying more of the investment-grade market, Oracle is one notch above junk at S&P, and a large leveraged refinancing struggled to clear without substantially better terms.

## Strong Data Check the Disinflation Rally

The day’s U.S. releases showed an economy with firm current momentum but uneven sector breadth. Advance retail and food-service sales rose 0.2% in June to $768.6 billion and were 6.7% higher than a year earlier. May’s monthly increase was revised to 1% from 0.9%, strengthening the comparison base and making June’s modest headline less suggestive of a broad consumer retreat.

The composition mattered. Sales excluding motor vehicles fell 0.2%, but sales excluding gasoline increased 0.7%, and the measure excluding both autos and gasoline rose 0.4%. Motor-vehicle dealers and nonstore retailers each recorded 1.9% gains, while gasoline-station receipts fell 5.3% and food-service sales increased only 0.1%. Lower gasoline receipts depressed the headline without showing that discretionary demand had weakened across the board.

Labor data offered another near-term resilience signal. Initial unemployment claims declined by 8,000 to 208,000 in the week ended July 11, from a revised 216,000. Their four-week average fell by 4,750 to 214,250. Continuing claims dropped by 16,000 to 1.805 million in the week ended July 4, although their four-week average increased slightly to 1.811 million. The insured unemployment rate held at 1.2%. Falling new and continuing claims gave the Fed little evidence that restrictive rates had produced an abrupt deterioration in employment.

The Philadelphia Fed survey delivered the strongest current-growth result. Its general activity index jumped to 41.4 in July from 10.3, the highest in nearly five years. New orders rose to 37 from 27.3, shipments climbed to 33.7 from 14.9, and the employment and average-workweek indexes remained positive at 10 and 14, respectively.

Price measures did not share the improvement in June’s national inflation reports. The prices-paid index increased to 53.9 from 53.2, while prices received rose to 27.4 from 20.3. Forward indicators were less emphatic than the current readings: expected activity over the next 6 months fell to 34.4 from 50.2, and planned capital spending declined to 30.1 from 41.2. The survey therefore strengthened the current demand and pipeline-price case without showing that manufacturers expected the same acceleration to persist.

May business data also pointed to strong nominal throughput. Manufacturing and trade sales increased 2.1% from April and 11.9% from a year earlier to $2.135 trillion. Inventories rose only 0.3% on the month and 3.1% on the year to $2.736 trillion, lowering the inventory-to-sales ratio to 1.28 from 1.39 a year earlier. Faster sales than stock accumulation suggested that current activity was not being sustained by an involuntary inventory buildup.

Housing remained the clearest counterweight. The NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index fell 2 points to 34 after June was revised to 36, extending its run below 40 to 15 months, the longest since 2012. Current sales declined to 37, expectations for the next 6 months fell to 43, and prospective-buyer traffic slipped to 23. Thirty-seven percent of builders cut prices, with an average reduction of 6%, while 63% used sales incentives. Financing costs and affordability were still constraining a rate-sensitive sector even as consumers, factories and the labor market held up.

The mix explains why Treasury yields rose only marginally rather than reversing the inflation-driven rally. Stronger activity increases the cost of keeping policy restrictive for less time than markets had begun to assume, but the releases did not overturn the softer CPI and PPI readings. Housing was weak, forward manufacturing expectations moderated, and the retail headline was held down partly by cheaper gasoline rather than a generalized collapse or acceleration in spending.

Rate-option positioning reflected that distinction. Selling of September and December options that benefit from higher policy rates continued during U.S. trading, with prior open-interest declines indicating that traders were closing earlier hedges rather than simply establishing new positions. The probability of a July increase remained low, while the amount of tightening priced by December fell to about 29 basis points from 43 basis points at the start of the week. The market was reducing the conviction and speed of the hiking path, not replacing it with an easing cycle.

Logan challenged that benign interpretation most directly. The Dallas Fed president, who votes on the Federal Open Market Committee this year, said modestly higher rates would better balance the risks because inflation did not appear to be returning sustainably to 2%. She acknowledged that June inflation had improved and that further moderation in housing and non-housing services could produce a more favorable outcome. Her objection was that this path depended on avoiding renewed energy pressure in the near term and stronger demand later.

That qualification was material after the week’s rebound in crude and Thursday’s activity figures. Logan said one month of relief was insufficient and argued that the demand effects of artificial-intelligence investment were already present, while the size and timing of its productivity benefits remained uncertain. Her reasoning joined the AI capital-spending boom to the reaction function through current demand for equipment, construction, power and labor rather than assuming that future productivity would immediately offset those pressures.

Schmid delivered a separate warning. The Kansas City Fed president described inflation as his primary concern and said price pressure extended beyond energy into a broad basket of goods and services, including food. He regarded the better June data as insufficient to establish a trend and argued that strong demand, not supply shocks alone, had to be considered when deciding whether inflation would persist. At the same time, he described the labor market as balanced and growth as resilient, reinforcing the case that the Fed could focus on prices without responding to an employment break.

Vice Chair Philip Jefferson added a more conditional signal in remarks released after the completed fixed-income close. He judged policy well positioned to support employment while inflation declined, but said the stance could be reconsidered if actual inflation did not begin to cool soon. Jefferson emphasized that AI could create opposing demand and supply shocks and that the timing of each mattered for policy. He also identified the possibility that the energy shock could feed longer-term expectations as a critical risk. His comments did not drive the completed Treasury close, but they broadened the group of officials preserving a route to higher rates if June’s improvement fails to continue.

Treasury cash activity declined alongside the small yield move. FINRA recorded $905.3 billion of par transactions across 326,681 trades, 14.7% less par activity than on July 15. Nominal-coupon activity fell 19.1% to $682 billion. Turnover declined 29.9% in maturities longer than 3 years and no more than 5 years, and 15.9% in the sector longer than 7 years and no more than 10 years. Those are two-way activity measures, but they distinguish Thursday’s modest retracement from the heavier engagement surrounding the earlier inflation repricing.

Front-end supply continued to find cash demand. Treasury’s $110 billion 4-week bill auction stopped at a 3.660% high rate with a 2.57 bid-to-cover ratio, while the $100 billion 8-week sale cleared at 3.650% with 2.84 times cover. Indirect bidders received $54.949 billion of accepted competitive tenders in the shorter auction and $65.470 billion in the longer one. Both issues settle July 21. Without a when-issued reference, the results do not establish rich or cheap pricing, but they showed no obvious funding strain as the coupon market debated the policy path.

## Korea Tightens as Japan’s Inflation Expectations Rise

South Korea began a new tightening cycle, raising its 7-day repurchase rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% in a unanimous decision. The increase was the first since January 2023 and matched every forecast in Bloomberg’s economist survey. It followed four reductions since late 2024, making the move a reversal in policy direction rather than a continuation of an established hiking campaign.

Governor Shin Hyun Song maintained a tightening bias but did not signal the timing of the next increase or an eventual peak. He said every coming meeting remained live and linked further action to incoming evidence on inflation, growth and financial stability. The swaps market priced at least two additional increases over the following 6 months, but Shin did not endorse an accelerated schedule.

The economic justification extended beyond headline inflation. Shin said the Bank of Korea’s May forecast of 2.6% growth for 2026 appeared too low and would be revised substantially higher in August because exports, investment and consumption were stronger than expected. The government had already lifted its forecast to 3%, while the International Monetary Fund raised its projection to 2.6%, the largest upward revision among 30 major economies.

Consumer inflation reached 3.2% in June, the fastest in more than 2 years, and the government expected it to average 2.6% for the year. Shin said the weak won would continue to lift import prices and that stronger activity could produce additional demand-driven inflation. A semiconductor-led export boom had pushed the current-account surplus for the first 5 months of 2026 above the record total for all of 2025, while the economy expanded 1.8% in Q1.

The central bank views the chip cycle as more structural than previous export upswings because AI demand is turning semiconductors into infrastructure rather than a conventional finished product. Shin said chip prices were more informative for Korea’s terms of trade and growth than short-term changes in chip-company shares. That distinction was especially relevant on Thursday, when global semiconductor equities sold off even though TSMC reported a 77% increase in quarterly profit and raised its outlook.

The benefits remain uneven. Employment has stayed weak despite the export boom, and capital-intensive semiconductor production has generated fewer jobs than its output would normally imply. Financial-stability concerns have also strengthened the case for tighter policy: Seoul apartment prices have risen for 76 consecutive weeks, household borrowing is accelerating again, and officials have warned that leveraged investment could amplify imbalances.

Korean bonds rallied after the decision and press conference. The 3-year yield fell 4 basis points to 3.83%, and the 10-year also declined 4 basis points to 4.29%. The reaction was consistent with a move that was expected and guidance that preserved quarterly or data-dependent tightening rather than promising a faster sequence. A hike can coexist with falling yields when investors had prepared for a more aggressive signal.

Japan provided a related inflation-expectations warning. Households expected annual inflation to average 10.8% over the next 5 years, the highest reading in Bank of Japan data extending back to 2006, although the median remained 5%. BOJ Executive Director Koji Nakamura reiterated that upside risks were high and that delaying policy adjustment could ultimately weigh on the economy. The benchmark rate was 1% after reaching its highest level since 1995 in June, and traders assigned about a 66% chance to another increase by October.

The survey also showed the cost of normalization. Twenty-four percent of households regarded interest rates as already too high, the largest share on record. The BOJ must therefore weigh unusually elevated perceived inflation against growing sensitivity to borrowing costs. Its next decision is scheduled for July 31.

Japan’s front-end auctions supplied realized demand measures without resolving that policy balance. The 1-year Treasury discount-bill auction accepted ¥2.136 trillion of competitive bids and ¥664.4 billion of noncompetitive bids. The lowest accepted price of 98.801 corresponded to a 1.2168% yield, while the weighted-average yield was 1.2066%; 73.8823% was allotted at the lowest price. The securities are issued July 21 and mature July 20, 2027.

A separate liquidity-enhancement operation accepted ¥699 billion across outstanding JGBs with 1 to 5 years remaining. Competitive bids totaled ¥2.679 trillion. The highest accepted spread was minus 0.001%, with 70.1674% allotted there, and the average accepted spread was minus 0.004%. The result showed demand for seasoned securities across eligible 2-, 5-, 10-, 20- and 30-year issues rather than providing a new benchmark-yield signal.

UK data presented a softer policy mix. Real gross domestic product rose 0.1% in May after a revised 0.1% decline in April. Output increased 0.7% over the 3 months through May and 1.1% from the same period a year earlier. Services grew 0.3% on the month, but production contracted 0.5% and construction fell 0.8%, leaving the recovery dependent on services rather than broadly distributed.

Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden argued that weak activity and labor-market slack reduced the danger that renewed energy inflation would become embedded in wages and domestic prices. She had voted with the majority to keep the policy rate at 3.75% for the previous 3 meetings and had favored reductions before the war. Breeden said she would support higher rates if a price feedback loop developed, but did not regard the oil shock alone as sufficient when borrowing costs were already restraining households and companies. The May output composition supported her caution even as Brent’s weekly rise kept the second-round risk alive.

## AI Borrowing Raises the Credit Bar

Oracle placed the financing strain from AI investment directly into the investment-grade market. S&P Global Ratings cut the company to BBB-, one notch above speculative grade, as a $250 billion data-center expansion consumed cash faster than revenue arrived. Moody’s maintained a negative outlook, leaving open the possibility of another downgrade over the medium term.

The timing mismatch is unusually large. Oracle burned more than $20 billion after capital expenditure over the latest 4 quarters, and S&P estimated that its free-cash-flow deficit could widen to $42 billion in the coming fiscal year. Capital spending is expected to keep rising through at least fiscal 2029. The company has accumulated a substantial contract backlog, but the revenue will be recognized over time while construction and equipment require cash upfront.

Oracle’s bonds already reflected more risk than the rating label alone suggested. Its 10-year debt yielded about 6.4%, close to the 6.7% yield on comparable BB paper and well above the 5.7% level of the 10-year BBB curve. A fall to junk at 2 rating agencies could make Oracle the largest issuer in the smaller U.S. high-yield market, potentially increasing its borrowing cost and forcing a new investor base to absorb the debt.

The company said maintaining investment grade remained its highest capital-allocation priority. It expects to raise about $40 billion through debt and equity this fiscal year, including a previously announced $20 billion at-the-market equity program. Oracle sold $25 billion of investment-grade bonds in February and has about $117 billion included in the Bloomberg U.S. Corporate Bond Index, making it the second-largest nonfinancial constituent after Amazon.

Concentration compounds the funding issue. S&P estimated that roughly half of Oracle’s $638 billion of remaining performance obligations were tied to OpenAI. That backlog offers a future revenue path but exposes the financing plan to a single large customer and to the pace at which contracted AI demand becomes cash flow. Alphabet and Meta have greater capacity to fund investment internally, while Oracle may need to reduce capital spending, issue more equity or accept additional leverage.

The broader bond index is becoming more exposed to the same cycle. Hyperscaler debt represents about 4% to 5% of investment-grade market value, depending on whether privately placed securities are included. Because those companies often issue longer debt at wider spreads, Barclays calculated that they account for 8.3% of the index’s duration-times-spread risk. Including a wider group of AI-related issuers raises the share to 11.4%, more than the contribution of the six large banks that have traditionally dominated issuance.

That risk footprint makes the AI financing cycle difficult for benchmarked investors to ignore. Additional technology supply must compete with banks, industrial companies and governments for a finite pool of duration capacity. Strongly rated hyperscaler bonds can offer attractive carry, but continued surprise issuance may require larger concessions and can lift clearing spreads beyond technology borrowers themselves.

Cotality showed how quickly the financing bar rises when leverage and cash flow are weaker. The property-data company was considering increasing the yield on part of a $5.3 billion refinancing after demand fell short. The proposed first-lien bond yield could rise to as much as 9.5% from the mid-8% area, while a second-lien tranche could move to about 12% from 11% and be issued below par. Investors were also discussing stronger documentation protections, though no final changes had been made.

The company carries debt equal to about 8 times earnings and is rated 6 notches below investment grade by S&P. It held about $55 million of cash at March 31 and was expected to rely on a revolving facility as free cash flow remained very modest. The transaction, intended to refinance debt used for its $6 billion acquisition by Stone Point Capital and Insight Partners, had initially been expected to price Thursday. The delay and prospective concessions showed that large leveraged deals could not rely on the broadly tight credit environment to overcome weak liquidity and aggressive leverage.

Aston Martin creditors were preparing for a different form of financing risk. Funds led by Arini Capital Management, BlackRock and Sculptor Capital Management hired Jefferies as adviser amid concern that new borrowing could subordinate existing claims under relatively loose bond documents. The group holds a majority of the company’s $1.85 billion-equivalent of bonds due in 2029, signed a cooperation agreement, and offered to discuss fresh financing and the wider capital structure.

Aston Martin received £50 million of shareholder debt in April after relying previously on equity injections to support liquidity. Product delays, quality problems, weak Chinese demand and U.S. tariffs have increased creditor concern that further financing might use collateral or structural provisions to disadvantage current bondholders. The engagement is preparatory rather than an agreed restructuring, but it moves the issue from general balance-sheet concern toward organized creditor action.

Chicago’s effort to monetize overdue parking fines also stalled. Bank of America stopped working as placement agent on a proposed sale of about $1 billion of receivables after the parties could not agree on the scope of services. The plan was intended to raise at least $89 million and help close the city’s budget gap, but officials cited privacy, legal and reputational risks for potential buyers. Its lack of progress contributed to a projected $90 million midyear revenue shortfall, even as several tax collections were running ahead of plan.

Broad listed credit prices were comparatively stable. LQD fell 0.07%, HYG declined 0.01%, JNK rose 0.01%, and EMB lost 0.15%. Those small moves did not indicate a generalized repricing comparable with the semiconductor selloff. The more consequential signal lay in issuer-level terms: a highly leveraged refinancing needed substantially more yield, Oracle’s AI expansion had consumed its rating cushion, and creditors at Aston Martin were organizing before any new transaction could weaken their position.

## War Risk Widens the Sovereign Divide

Renewed U.S.-Iran fighting had a more direct effect on Middle Eastern sovereign credit than on Treasury inflation compensation. The average regional sovereign spread widened about 20 basis points in the week after President Donald Trump warned that the ceasefire might be over, reaching 402 basis points over Treasuries. That was the widest since October 2022 and contributed to the fastest year-to-date spread increase since 2018.

Middle Eastern dollar bonds became the worst-performing regional group in emerging markets since the war began. Governments in the region offered 163 basis points of additional yield over other developing-country sovereigns. The repricing reversed part of the more than 50-basis-point narrowing that followed the tentative April ceasefire.

The security situation deteriorated again Thursday. The United States struck a sanctioned supertanker near Iran’s main oil terminal, its first attack on a vessel there since reinstating the blockade. Observable commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz was sparse and largely limited to Iran-linked vessels using a northern route approved by Tehran. India ordered shipowners to stop assigning its seafarers to voyages through the strait, and Asian spot liquefied-natural-gas prices rose to their highest since March.

Crude nevertheless declined modestly at the New York close after a large three-day advance. Brent remained up 10.39% over a week and WTI 9.53%, so the daily fall did not restore the pre-escalation energy backdrop. The dollar index gained 0.23%, gold futures fell 1.44% to $3,985.60, and the VIX rose 6.76% to 16.73. Higher yields and a firmer dollar outweighed geopolitical demand for gold, while equity volatility was concentrated most visibly in technology.

Senegal illustrated a sovereign problem driven less by external liquidity than by fiscal solvency. Citigroup estimated that dollar-bond holders could recover 43 cents to 50 cents on the dollar under a restructuring, assuming exit yields of 11% and 9%, respectively. Existing bonds traded between 51 and 54 cents, with the 2048 note quoted at 51.70 cents in London, placing market prices above the lower end of Citi’s scenarios.

Debt stands near 130% of gross domestic product, and the International Monetary Fund program is suspended. Authorities remain broadly opposed to restructuring, but Lazard’s appointment as financial adviser and weakening demand for longer regional-market securities have intensified speculation that negotiations may become necessary. Senegal’s spread was almost 1,500 basis points over Treasuries, the highest distress level among African sovereign issuers in JPMorgan’s index.

Citi distinguished Senegal from Zambia and Ghana because its immediate problem is fiscal and debt sustainability rather than a balance-of-payments shortage. That difference does not make a restructuring less costly for bondholders. The bank judged that a large nominal haircut would be required if Senegal remained committed to an IMF-supported adjustment, while domestic politics would influence whether talks begin this year.

The turn in long-duration sentiment also extended beyond distressed borrowers. Hoisington Investment Management, known for a bullish Treasury stance maintained over more than 3 decades, said larger fiscal deficits, heavier capital demand and a higher long-run inflation range now pointed toward rising long yields. The effective duration of its portfolio fell from 20.88 years at the end of September to 4.7 years at the end of March and to less than 1 year by June 30.

Hoisington placed long-run inflation equilibrium around 3.5% to 4.5%, with a meaningful risk of episodes above 5%, and argued that investors were demanding more term premium from Treasury debt. Its assessment is a portfolio manager’s structural view rather than a description of Thursday’s small move. It is nevertheless consistent with the market’s continuing reluctance to push the 30-year yield decisively below 5% even after favorable June inflation data. The long bond ended at 5.084%, while the modest daily rise left it 10.4 basis points higher over the month.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. data sequence arrives July 17. June import and export prices and housing starts are due at 08:30 ET, followed by industrial production and capacity utilization at 09:15 and preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment at 10:00. Trade prices will show whether energy, shipping and tariff costs are passing through before reaching consumer inflation. Housing starts will test whether weak builder confidence is appearing in construction activity, while industrial production will show whether the Philadelphia Fed’s surge is part of a broader factory acceleration.

Michigan’s inflation-expectations measures are especially important after Fed officials emphasized the risk that the renewed energy shock becomes persistent. A stable expectations reading would support the market’s decision not to rebuild 10-year inflation compensation on Thursday. A rise alongside firm sentiment and production would strengthen Logan’s and Schmid’s concern that June’s favorable inflation results may not survive stronger demand and higher delivered energy costs.

Final June euro-area harmonized inflation is scheduled for July 17 at 11:00 CEST. The composition will matter for the European Central Bank’s July 23 decision because officials are assessing whether higher energy prices are broadening into goods, services or wage setting. The ECB’s bank lending survey on July 21 will add evidence on second-quarter lending standards, loan demand and banks’ expectations for Q3 before the rate announcement and press conference.

China sets its 1- and 5-year loan prime rates on July 20 at 09:00 CST. The fixings follow weak property and investment data and will show whether policymakers are willing to transmit easier financing conditions through bank lending rates. Japan’s 3-month bill auction on July 17 will test near-term yen cash demand, but the larger duration event is the approximately ¥300 billion reopening of a 40-year JGB on July 22. That sale comes as household inflation expectations reach a record, the BOJ retains a tightening bias and more households report that rates already feel too high.

U.S. Treasury supply returns with $92 billion of 13-week bills and $79 billion of 26-week bills on July 20, both settling July 23, followed by a $95 billion 6-week bill sale on July 21. The long-duration test is the July 22 reopening of $13 billion of 20-year bonds at 13:00 ET. The 5% coupon security settles July 24 and matures May 15, 2046. The auction will test demand for term risk while the 30-year yield remains above 5% and private AI borrowing competes for duration capacity.

Corporate execution will provide a parallel measure. Cotality’s proposed refinancing has already moved from the mid-8% area toward as much as 9.5% on first-lien debt, with potential document improvements and a still-higher second-lien yield. Whether the company can complete the $5.3 billion transaction—and on what final protections—will indicate how much concession highly leveraged borrowers need even when broad credit funds are little changed.

The U.S.-Iran conflict remains the most immediate threat to the market’s distinction between softer realized inflation and firmer prospective inflation. Sparse Hormuz traffic and the strike near Iran’s export terminal have not yet produced another daily surge in crude, but Brent and WTI remain roughly 10% higher over the week. Continued disruption would affect later inflation data, corporate margins and sovereign risk even if the Fed holds rates on July 29.

For Treasuries, the central test is no longer whether the June CPI and PPI reports removed most of the case for a July increase; market pricing already reflects that judgment. The question is whether resilient consumption, low claims and strong current factory activity allow officials to preserve or deliver tightening later in the year. Further broad disinflation and anchored expectations would validate the small July 16 yield retracement. Renewed price breadth, sustained energy pressure or another sequence of firm activity readings would make the current combination—low near-term hike probability but more than one quarter-point priced by December—harder to maintain.

section_summaries.market_read: Higher real yields, lower breakevens and a nearly parallel curve move pointed to growth resilience rather than renewed inflation fear.
section_summaries.summary: Firm U.S. activity and inflation-focused Fed commentary nudged Treasury yields higher but reversed little of the rally generated by softer June inflation. Markets distinguished a low-probability July increase from continued tightening risk later in the year, while AI financing concerns weighed on technology shares and raised questions for corporate bond supply.

section_summaries.market_read: Markets reduced the speed and conviction of the hiking path without replacing it with an easing cycle.
section_summaries.section_title: Strong Data Check the Disinflation Rally
section_summaries.summary: June retail sales, falling jobless claims and a 41.4 Philadelphia Fed index showed firm current momentum, while housing remained weak and manufacturers’ forward expectations moderated. Logan and Schmid said broad price pressure and resilient demand kept higher rates possible, but the mixed evidence supported only a small Treasury retracement.

section_summaries.market_read: An expected hike can coexist with lower yields when guidance is less aggressive than investors had prepared for.
section_summaries.next_check: The BOJ decides policy on July 31.
section_summaries.section_title: Korea Tightens as Japan’s Inflation Expectations Rise
section_summaries.summary: The Bank of Korea raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 2.75% as growth, inflation and financial-stability risks strengthened, yet Korean bonds rallied because the move was expected and guidance did not promise faster tightening. In Japan, record household inflation expectations supported the BOJ’s tightening bias even as more households said rates already felt too high.

section_summaries.market_read: Heavy technology issuance can raise clearing concessions beyond AI borrowers as it competes for finite duration capacity.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Borrowing Raises the Credit Bar
section_summaries.summary: S&P cut Oracle to BBB- as its $250 billion data-center expansion widened cash-flow deficits and increased dependence on external funding. The broader AI buildout is also taking a larger share of investment-grade duration capacity, while Cotality’s delayed $5.3 billion refinancing showed that weak liquidity and high leverage still require substantial concessions.

section_summaries.market_read: Geopolitical stress was more visible in regional sovereign credit than in Treasury inflation compensation.
section_summaries.section_title: War Risk Widens the Sovereign Divide
section_summaries.summary: Renewed U.S.-Iran fighting and sparse Hormuz traffic widened Middle Eastern sovereign spreads even as crude declined at the New York close. Senegal faced a separate fiscal-solvency problem, while Hoisington’s retreat from long-duration Treasuries reflected concern that deficits, capital demand and a higher inflation range would sustain term premium.

The central Treasury test is whether anchored inflation expectations and further disinflation can coexist with resilient demand, or whether firm activity and sustained energy pressure preserve tightening later this year. U.S. data, long-duration auctions, leveraged refinancing terms and Hormuz disruption provide the next observable evidence.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries give back little of the disinflation rally despite resilient U.S. demand
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries edged lower, but the nearly parallel move was restrained: the 2-year yield rose 0.6 basis point to 4.142%, the 10-year added 0.5 basis point to 4.554%, and the 30-year increased 0.4 basis point to 5.084%. Retail sales, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey showed resilient demand, while Lorie Logan and Jeff Schmid warned that one favorable inflation month was insufficient. Even so, swaps priced only about 3 basis points of tightening for July 29, versus around 29 basis points by December.

The 10-year real yield rose 1 basis point while its breakeven rate fell 0.5 basis point, showing that investors demanded more inflation-adjusted return without rebuilding inflation compensation. Oil declined at the close despite remaining roughly 10% higher over the week amid renewed U.S.-Iran fighting and disrupted Hormuz traffic.

AI financing supplied a separate risk signal. Semiconductor shares fell sharply as concern grew over the scale and uncertain payoff of spending, while Oracle’s rating cushion narrowed and Cotality’s leveraged refinancing required substantially better proposed terms.
overall_summary.summary: Treasury yields rose only marginally as strong retail, labor and factory data and inflation-focused Fed comments preserved the prospect of tightening later this year without restoring a compelling case for a July increase.
